query: From these 20 inbox and chat observations, decide which deserve my attention today.
Turn this noisy feature request into a bounded change set with acceptance criteria.
Investigate GitHub issue #210 in the repo and draft a response to it.
Review the diff in this pull request and tell me whether the change is correct.
Send my reply in that Slack thread now.
Pull the last week of messages from #support in Slack.
Triage this customer's question against our product docs and route it to a specialist if it needs one.
Update our CRM from what the prospect said on this call.
Summarise the minutes from this meeting transcript.
Write a polite email declining a meeting invitation.
Review this email conversation with the customer and prepare the next response.
Here's the Slack thread with the client. Draft a reply, but don't send it.
Read this support thread and tell me whether the customer is actually asking for a code change. If so, quote the exact request.
What's the next useful action on this conversation? It might only need a follow-up task.
Go through this chat thread and decide: reply, follow-up, coding request, or nothing to do.
Prepare an unsent follow-up for this partner email thread. It's gone quiet for two weeks.
This thread looks truncated. Review it and tell me what's missing before you'd draft anything.
Review the conversation in this source packet and propose its reply on the routes we configured.
Did anyone in this email exchange ask us to build something? If so, flag it for engineering intake.
Draft my reply to this thread with the vendor, keeping to what the messages actually say.
Go through these three customer threads and prepare what each one needs next, a reply, a follow-up or a coding handoff. Don't send anything.
